The Spanish football champions are the winners of [[La Liga]], the primary football competition in [[Spain]]. The league is contested on a [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] basis, with the title awarded to the team that finishes top at the end of the season. First established in 1929 with ten teams, La Liga has featured 20 teams since 1997. Before the league's formation, the [[Copa del Rey]]—a regionalised cup competition—was effectively considered the national championship.<ref>{{cite book|last=Cresswell |page=489 |title=European Football, A Fan's Handbook}}</ref> The league was suspended between 1936 and 1939 due to the [[Spanish Civil War]].<ref name="champions">{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanchamp.html |title=Spain – List of Champions |date=4 September 2008 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=29 November 2008 }}</ref>

[[Real Madrid]] is the most successful club, with 36 league titles, followed by [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] with 29. Barcelona has won the [[Double (association football)|double]] (winning the league and cup in the same season) a record nine times, ahead of [[Athletic Bilbao]]’s five.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/doublerec.html |title=Doing the Double! |date=27 November 2008 |publisher=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=29 November 2008 }}</ref> Barcelona is also one of only two [[UEFA|European]] clubs—alongside [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], who joined them in [[2019–20 FC Bayern Munich season|2020]]—to have won the [[Treble (association football)|treble]] twice, most recently in [[2014–15 FC Barcelona season|2015]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Kevin |last=Ashby |title=Guardiola salutes his treble winners |url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/fixturesresults/round=15280/match=302813/report=rw.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090529075133/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/fixturesresults/round=15280/match=302813/report=rw.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=29 May 2009 |publisher=[[UEFA|Union of European Football Associations]] |date=27 May 2009 |access-date=28 May 2009 }}</ref> The current champions are Barcelona, who claimed their 29th title in the [[2025–26 La Liga|2025–26]] season.

The three lowest-placed teams in La Liga are relegated to the [[Segunda División]] and replaced by the top three from that division. Of the league’s founding clubs, only Athletic Bilbao, Barcelona, and Real Madrid have never been relegated.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/04/08/sports/08iht-SOCCER.4.5190989.html?_r=1 |first=Rob |last=Hughes |title=Athletic Bilbao gets an Easter gift |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=8 April 2007 |access-date=4 December 2008 }}</ref>
